title: How to Store Potatoes and Onions So They Last 3x Longer
desc: Potatoes and onions both hate light and moisture, which is why they rot so fast in a plastic bag or the fridge. Keep them dry, dark and ventilated, and keep the two apart so the onions do not make the potatoes sprout. Open-sided bamboo bins on the counter do all three, and the wood lids block light. Tap to see the stackable set.

title: The Pantry Setup That Keeps Produce Fresh All Week
desc: The trick is airflow plus visibility. If you cannot see it, you will not eat it, and it rots in the back. A three-tier open bamboo rack gives every vegetable its own level, keeps the greens on top, roots below, and lets you grab things without unloading the shelf. Tap to see the rack.

title: Fruit Basket Styling for a Clutter-Free Counter
desc: Skip the bowl. One deep bowl turns into a pile, and the fruit at the bottom bruises under everything else. A stackable basket with a wood lid keeps a single layer on show, hides the rest, and gives you back counter space. Ripe fruit on top, bananas hung outside. Tap to see the basket.

title: The 3-Tier Basket Hack That Doubles Counter Space
desc: If your counter is one square metre, stop storing sideways. A three-tier wire basket gives you the same footprint with three usable levels: onions and garlic down low, potatoes in the middle, fruit on top where you can actually reach it. Nothing is stacked, nothing is hidden. Tap to see the basket.

title: Stop Losing Vegetables to the Back of the Pantry
desc: Most produce is thrown away, not eaten. The fix is one rule: nothing hides behind anything. Stackable bins with bamboo tops let you pull the whole row forward in one move, so the squash from last week is still in your line of sight. Two bins, one shelf, no more science experiments in the dark. Tap to see the set.
